utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, let's look at a document which was proceeded to you yesterday and I assume you had a chance to read. It's some excerpts from a book. I don't know if you have them there in front of you. You're shaking your head yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- and this has been provided. It's starting with tab 1. If you could just look at tab 1, please. This is a book -- could you read the title for me please of the book?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Phoenixes of Freedom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a book -- you're familiar with this book. It's a collection of books; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please. Yes, now we can go on. That is problem here with the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe if the usher --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you hear me now okay?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're familiar with this book. It's actually a collection of several books.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it. I saw it last night for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're familiar with the project to write these books; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard about this project, such a project, and I may say that, yes. But this book, I had never read it before. I saw it last night for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony is you only heard about this project?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said about the book, that I had not read the book, while --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The project, though, you were aware of the project to write those books; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some initiatives. I don't know if you can hear me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can hear you. In fact, you sign the approval for the book; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you turn to the -- if you turn to the third page of tab 1, you'll see where you signed. You see your name about halfway there? That's your signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your testimony is that until last night you had not read these selections?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor -- this is a project, Your Honours, to set up an editing board for this project. But I did not read the book. So this was about the board, but I have not read the book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Last night you had a chance to read these excerpts?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If -- if we could turn to the first one. It's at tab 2, which is about Sadik Shala. Sadik Shala is your nephew; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- before he was killed in Rahovec on the 19th of July.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you, please, to turn to the second page --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th, yes. Sorry, Mr. Prosecutor. Before we go on, I have marked those -- some of the pages. I have underlined some excerpts. I don't know whether this is a mistake, whether this is wrong. Maybe it is not allowed here. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's no problem with marking it, but if you could just focus on my questions, please. If you could turn to the second page. It's page 210 on the Albanian, and it's the second page of the English, and I just want to read you -- it's -- on the Albanian it's -- I believe it's the last paragraph of the Albanian, and it says: "On 21 March 1998, the KLA cell was formed in Klecka. The first unit of this cell was named Celiku, which consisted of Fatmir Limaj, Celiku; Ismet Jashari, Kumanova; Haxhi Shala, Topi; and Sadik Shala with his brothers Nexhmi, Sabit and Bajram. You're turning red, Mr. Limaj.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I said you're turning -- when I was reading that you're turning red.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm sorry. No. There is no reason to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is true, isn't it, on the 21st of March when you arrived in Klecka this cell, this first unit, the Celiku unit was formed, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes. The cell -- the creation of the cell is the 21st of March, but it got the name Celiku later on. Well, about what you said about getting red, blushing, there are mistakes here. There are things that are wrong here, even fatal mistakes I must say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the passage I just read, though, that's correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are grave mistakes here, and I need to speak about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's focus --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are mistakes. There are inconsistencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, let's just focus on the passage I read. The passage I read is true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 21st of March, the cell was there, yes. Three of us were in this cell, and later on it turned into the Celiku unit. And after that Celiku 1 and Celiku 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was Celiku already in March of 1998.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were Celiku and the unit was Celiku.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. No, and I can argue against what you're saying. It's not true. The truth is different. By the end of April, it got the name Celiku. We got two radios, two radios to communicate with each other, and then we got the name Celiku because we had to communicate with each other as Celiku 1 and Celiku 2. It was not true until April, until the end of April. We were a unit, and my nephews joined the unit with -- there were five of us later, but it was not the Celiku unit until the end of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Limaj, I'm going to suggest that you're pushing forward the dates. Once again another example of pushing forward the dates. That's what you're doing, aren't you? Let's turn, please to --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. On the opposite. You are trying to describe here a reality that was not like that. The truth is different. You are trying to create something that did not exist. It was not like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain how that was -- how they got that -- the person who wrote that in this book got that wrong?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just taking an example. I have to explain here because when I say mistakes have been made, on the 8th of January, 1997, Sadik contacts the KLA and becomes a member of the KLA. 8th of January, 1997, Sadik manages to contact Fatmir Limaj and become a member of the KLA. While we saw in the film, Your Honours, where I said that I sent word to Skender, who is Sadik's brother that three people will come to your place. If that was not like that I couldn't have sent word to them. It's not true. What's said here is not true. It's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a typographical error, isn't it, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think this is a professional mistake made by the people who compiled this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just intervene for a moment? I haven't so far objected to this, but once again it would be helpful to know the provenance of the book, who actually wrote this passage. If it's going to be used to test the credibility of the witness which was the original objective of this, apparently, then for his credibility to be tested one needs to know a great deal more about this document and so far the comments that are being made regularly, whether it's his turning colour or his reaction to a particular passage and so on we say is not proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting, the provenance is an issue of materiality. If you would like to explore that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you were involved, were you not, in setting up the board to write this -- write these histories of these individuals; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not true, Your Honours. I don't know who the author of this book is. I know about the initiative. This was an initiative of the veterans of war and some historians to create a board that would collect all the materials about the martyrs in one place because people did not know who the martyrs were, where they were from, what they had done and so on. So that's why I supported this initiative to collect all these materials together. And we were ready to have consultations with them. And if they wanted to consult us, I expressed my willingness to help. But this is as far as it went. I never compiled or wrote or did anything in this book. Nobody came to consult me. And at that time you must know that there were several books that were published with all good intentions. There are many mistakes made here. I see mistakes here about Sadik and Ismet, but also about myself. There are mistakes here about what they say about me. Maybe they did not consult the people, the concrete people who were involved in order to write the things as they were. You have -- you have my picture there, and in one of the lines it says that "Fatmir Limaj was wounded on the 25th of June, 1998." I myself know when I was wounded, and there are proofs here that show when I was wounded. While here it says "Sadik, Fatmir and Ismet Jashari came in 1997." This is also a mistake, because I told you when we returned from Switzerland. So I don't know. To speak the truth, I don't know who the authors are, and they -- I can tell you that they did not consult me, and that's unfortunate, because there are serious mistakes that have been made here. But this is a concrete example, typical example that speaks about the fact that each person has his own truth in his mind, his own story in his mind, because the situation was so confused that everybody saw the situation in -- in their own eyes. And I'm expressing to you the way I saw the situation with my own eyes. With all their goodwill and all the best intentions they have made fatal mistakes here. There are several other examples here as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry to intervene. I do try to resist doing it. In view of the answer and the fact that this is all going to credibility, in my submission there can be no further use of this document. It's not a document he's compiled. It's not a document he's authored. It's not his document. I accept, obviously, if it was the question of credibility could be used further but at this stage I would submit that's the send of it. It's a collateral matter, and there should be no further questioning without that provenance being proved. And one final remark. As I understand it, it's no intention for this to be exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just -- I appreciate Mr. Mansfield's remarks. However, it is a published document, and the -- the point that Mr. Limaj has testified about is repeated again and again in the document, and I would just ask to have another question or two to pursue this matter and then I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean that you would be moving on to return to it for cross-examination on other matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No. I'd move on to another issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But you feel you have not exhausted this question of provenance; is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry on the issue of provenance I have no further questions. I have one or two further questions on what is actually in the text, because there is a repetition of the issue that we've been talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, in reviewing these excerpts about Sadik Shala, Ismet Jashari and Jete Hasani, you saw in all three excerpts it described the Celiku units as being set up in March of 1998; correct? Did you see that? Did you notice that? In all --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I noticed it. But it's not true, sir. There are catastrophic mistakes here, and I gave you an example here. This person who has written this had no idea about what went on. They said I was wounded in June of -- June 1998, but I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, your testimony is that this mistake is repeated again and again in the book, this same mistake?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. This is the -- not the only mistake. There are other mistakes as well, and this shows that the authors of this book have not had even elementary knowledge, not about Sadik, not about Kumanova and the organisation at that time. The biography is okay, but when they speak about the organisation, it shows that they had no clear view of the matters as they were at the time, and I gave you two or three examples that -- of their mistakes that show that their information was not correct. On the 21st of March, 1998, there was no unit named Celiku in the KLA. There wasn't. Of course they referred to Celiku units, and you have Jete Hasani here. He never was a soldier in the Celiku unit in Klecke. He was a member of the Kroimire unit. And Luani. And it speaks here about Kumanova getting wounded. He was wounded in April, and here it says 25th of June. He was wounded when we returned from Denica to Malisheve where here it says that here he was wounded in Dukadjin somewhere. And it says here that I was wounded in Loznica in Kijeve, which is wrong of course. So this shows that the author had the wrong information or the people he consulted did not have the right information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, let's go to -- let's talk about your pseudonym Celiku. You testified earlier and again today that it wasn't until the end of April that you even heard that name Celiku. You testified that on April 29th was the first time you heard that name Celiku.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I didn't say I heard. I said that Rexhep Selimi proposed at the end of April for us to have a code because he gave us the radios. And in fact, I told him that I would have liked the pseudonym Arbeni as a proposal, but -- there were other proposals at well but this was Rexhep's proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So before April 29th that name was not used is your testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. To my knowledge at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you said that even after April 29th, the soldiers did not know you as "Celiku" but continued to know you as "Daja." That was your testimony.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. This is not my testimony, because now again you want to make a confusion here. Allow me to explain this. It's not on the 29th of April but in the end of April, not the 29th as a date. Your Honours, I want to explain again. When we received the two radios, we met with Rexhep Selimi. He brought the two radios. When we received them, as a unit we had to have a name in order to be able to answer when speaking on the radio. I could not possibly answer as Fatmir or "Daja." And on that occasion Rexhep Selimi proposed what to do about the code. I suggested that I should use the name Albanian, and then he said no. Let's leave it Celiku. Your Honours, it was a coincidence. My brother Demir, in the Turkish language his name means steel, Celiku, in Albanian. So it was a coincidence that my pseudonym --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you've already told the story. But -- on the second day when you told the story, and it's at line 14 of page 13 of the uncorrected transcript, it says that this event that you're describing, you said, "I think this occurred on the 29th of April." That's where I got that date, the 29th of April. Are you now saying that's into the the date?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not saying that again. I'm stressing it again here. I cannot be correct with dates all the time. I cannot tell you the exact date. So that's why I'm telling you it should be the end of April, and I cannot determine the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. If we could just focus on this. You said -- you were asked by Mr. Mansfield by what name you were known at this period, May the 9th, and you said that you were known by the pseudonym "Daja."

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. That is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So can you explain, then, how it is that Sylejman Selimi testified that in April he knew you by the name Celiku, and Ramiz Qeriqi testified in April he knew you by the name Celiku. In this courtroom both testified this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to object again. These are really not questions capable of being answered by the witness. If he wants to say were you known by some other -- but to ask the witness whether he can explain what another witness meant or how the other witness came to know something, again, is not the proper way to go about the questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is some substance in that, Mr. Mansfield, but a slight reshaping of the question could make the point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, isn't it in fact true that in April, as Sylejman Selimi and Ramiz Qeriqi testified, you were known as Celiku to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true because at that time we did not have soldiers to know me by that name. I told you that we were only three or four. And the reason why they said so is that because after August, everyone knew me -- everyone in the world knew me by the name Celiku. And now I don't know about the phase, how they -- the time, how they learned and when they learned, but as Celiku the majority of them knew me. And in the end, I don't know why Sylej and Luan said that, because during this time we didn't even see each other, myself and Sylejman. Reality is different. This is not true. Let me explain here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I think you've answered the question, but just to be clear, your testimony is that these two other witnesses are mistaken about the dates and you are not. That's your -- that's a fair summary of your testimony, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be mistaken about myself, about my history, about things that I've experienced. This is an example of what can happen when the period is not specified. The truth is what I'm telling you, and the two of them have wronged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about the 9th of May, the battle in Lapusnik. The -- it's true, isn't it, that the following people participated in the battle of the 9th of May: Yourself, Isak Musliu, Ramiz Qeriqi, Sadik Shala, Ismet Jashari, Haxhi Shala, Sabit Shala, Shaban Shala, Nexhmi Shala, Ramiz Shala.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. No, that's not true. The truth is what I've said here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell me of those names which ones did not participate?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to you.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So after the attack was over, people did come there, but we were others who went there. Ramiz Qeriqi came by the end of attack. Ismet did not come because he was wounded in his leg. When we returned from Lapusnik we saw him in Berisha. He was wounded. Haxhi Shala, he came after the attack was completed. Shaban Shala I don't know for which Shaban Shala we are speaking about, but he wasn't there. Shaban Shala wasn't there in that action. It was myself, Isak; Sabit remained with the radio in Berisha. We were five. Myself, Isak, Sadik, Bardhi and Nexhmi Shala. These are the five people who participated in that attack. As for others, they came after the attack was completed. Many of others came, even civilians, but they did not participate in the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in charge of your unit; correct? In that 9th of May battle, you were in charge of the unit that came from Klecka to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it clearly here. Your Honours, I was the person who charge for my unit from Klecka, those five men. These were guests, young men that were passing from one zone into another. And from what we saw, from the developments on that road, we went out to see what was going on on the Gjurgjice-Orlat road. It was daytime. Sadik -- because he comes from that region because for myself it was the first time that I used that road, the road from Berisha. So Sadik took us there by vehicle and we followed the developments there. So we decided on the spot. We said let's go and we went. With Sadik and Nexhmi who was with us and he wasn't a soldier until that time, he joined us. Isak also came. He had come there with me to see what was going on. And a certain Bardhi who was from the village of Drenoc who had come to our base for a week until their base in his own territory was prepared. So when we saw the situation there, when we saw that the Serb forces had placed a bus as a kind of a shield, we decided to go downwards, downhill, and this is what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, that's a very long answer. My only question which you answered at the very beginning was that you were in charge of the unit. That was my only question. So if you could just keep your answers to just answering my question and then we'll get through this.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that Isak Musliu and Luan, Ramiz Qeriqi, just happened to be in Klecka that day.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move back in time for a moment about those two men. You also testified that you met them on one of your trips to Likovc in April of 1998; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you came back -- you went with them to Klecka at that time, and Sadik Shala. So it was you and Sadik Shala and Luan and Isak Musliu back to Klecka in April of 1998; right? You made that trip; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the first meet where they came with us yes. They came with us from Likovc and joined us on the way to Klecka. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you arrived to Klecka, Luan continued and went to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Together with Isak. Together with Isak they went. And at that time, to tell you the truth, I didn't know where they were going, whether they were going to Kroimire. I don't know when they were heading to but they went to their municipalities, to the municipalities where their villages belonged they went together and this is the first time I saw these persons. I saw the persons for the first time on this day. I never saw them before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony is that you didn't know that Luan was going to Kroimire to set up a KLA unit in Kroimire? You didn't know that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first day, I'm speaking now about the first day. We discussed it. We said that we would go to the villages, to birthplaces, birthplaces, to our native municipalities, so Lipjan and Stimlje are very broad municipalities. They might have gone to other places as well but it is true that they headed to their native municipalities. This was on the first day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after Luan went to Kroimire he returned within a few days. And he went back and forth between Kroimire and Klecka several times during that initial period; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a problem because you're going only halfway towards the truth. Let us go the whole way through. Not only Luan but also Isak. They came again to Klecka. They rested because, as I said, the trip was very tiring. They rested for some time in Klecke, and they had to continue their trip to Likovc because they had left some friends there who had come together with them from Germany. After they had secured a base to that place where they had went to secure a base, they were going to get them from Likovc and bring them to their respective territory. They spent a night at Klecka. They spent the entire following day in Klecka and in the evening they set off for Likovc and there was no need for us to escort them because they knew the road. This is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question so you've anticipated my next question. They came to Klecka and they went to Likovc and then they came back to Klecka again; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They returned from Likovc to Klecka. They had fetched two or three soldiers with them. Just a moment, please. They had fetched two or three soldiers with them, and it's around this time when the events at Lapusnik occurred. It is in this period of time. The event caught them there where I was, the events of Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified also on the second day of your testimony that during this time period in April you said that there were hundreds of soldiers who went through your base at that time.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I said so, then it's a mistake. What I meant is that during this time, through Klecka -- it's in the future, not in April. But after April not only hundreds but thousands of soldiers passed through Klecka. I apologise if I made a mistake in my earlier testimony. But in this time, if I'm not mistaken between 15 and 20 soldiers passed through Klecka. Mr. Prosecutor, at that time a certain Ymeri Ilazi came who passed to Jezerce with his group who went to Jezerce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just referring to -- it's on page 21 of the uncorrected transcript at line 14, and you're talking about when they were there on the 9th of May and you said they were at my base and not more than that. "People like Isak, hundreds of them passed through that base and later." That's what I'm referring to. At that time were there hundreds of --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not about the time period. I wanted just to give you an example that in the time after that, in May, June, November, December, many hundreds passed through to Llap, to Nerodime, to other parts of Drenica, to Karadak. And not only through Klecka but through other parts as well. But mostly through Klecka because it was a suitable place to go to the Nerodime zone and Karadak zone. But I'm not specifying the time period here. I just use it as an example when I said that people like Isak, young men like Isak, there were hundreds of them that passed through Klecka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there something wrong? Do you need something?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could go to the toilet, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn and return at five minutes to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If the witness could be shown Exhibit P153, please. And it's being put on the Sanction as well. The think the witness is having trouble with the microphone -- with the earphone. It pops out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you see this picture? It's Exhibit P153.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a picture of you, Luan, Kumanova and Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You agree that this is picture was taken in April of 1998 in Klecke?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be ascertained, but it can be clearer. It is clearly seen that I'm wounded, and I believe it's April. If we get a clearer picture, then we can clearly investigate that. Both me and Ismet were wounded, so I'm sure it must be April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think it is April.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the picture being taken?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I can't remember, but I know that up until then we hadn't taken any pictures. When Luan came, he had a camera with him. Until then, we didn't have a camera. And for the first time that we had a picture taken was taken then. Therefore, I suppose it's April. When he came in Germany, he had a camera with him. We didn't have. We didn't have uniforms. We had nothing when we came.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm done with that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, talking -- talking about Kroimire now, Ramadan Behluli testified in this courtroom that he was a soldier who joined the KLA in Kroimire on the 20th of April, 1998; that after he joined, he took orders from Luan in Kroimire; and that Luan -- he followed the orders and that Luan got orders from above. That's all true, isn't it, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor, that's not true. If you want to summarise, you may, but the truth is as follows: He -- that man knows better, but I know one thing. At the time, Ramiz Qeriqi, when he came to Klecke we had nothing but our weapons. What he did in Kroimire, what he organised and how things worked, I do not know. I'm talking about that time. That's why I'm saying I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Limaj, Luan, Ramiz Qeriqi, testified in that courtroom that by May of 1998 there was a chain of command that went from Likovc to Klecke to Kroimire. That's true, isn't it, that there was a chain of command from Likovc to Klecke to Kroimire and the other points?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember him saying things the way you're saying it. And if that's the case, that's not true. If you want, I can tell you another thing. Ramiz Qeriqi was directly connected with his friends, Your Honours, in Drenica who -- who were involved with the other movement before, and he was in direct communication with his friends in Drenica at the time. And that was even before coming to the liberation war. So it's not true that the network worked in the way you described it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony -- your testimony is that there was no -- at this time, by May of 1998, there was not a chain of command that went from Likovc to Klecke to Kroimire. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such chain of command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in -- in his interview which is now in evidence as P160, Shukri Buja said that he would get orders from you, and when you didn't know what to do you would consult with the General Staff in this time period, in May -- May of --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not understanding what you say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat it.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll repeat it. In the interview that is now -- that Shukri Buja gave, which is now in evidence as P160, he said that in this time period he would get orders from you, and when you didn't know what to do you would consult with the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Absolutely. I can provide a hundred thousand arguments, Your Honours, that prove the contrary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I actually don't want arguments. I just want your evidence, okay? Just -- so if you can answer the questions. So you're saying that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never in my life have I given orders to Shukri Buja. On behalf of General Staff, yes, but individually, no, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did give orders to him on behalf of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I became a member of General Staff, yes, I have conveyed a decision of the General Staff, and that was part of what the General Staff had decided upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your testimony is that in April, May, June, and July you never gave orders to Shukri Buja?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never. Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- and you never gave orders to Luan. That's also your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Luan it's something different. When the brigade was set up, was established in August, I was his brigade commander, and from August I issued orders to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April, May, June, and July, your testimony is you never gave orders --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No chain of command from Likovc to Klecke to Kroimire. That's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never at that time. It did not exist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning now to following -- the period following the 9th of May battle. You testified that in May of 1998, after the 9th of May battle, you went to Lapusnik on two other occasions when there was fighting, once on the 17th or 18th of May, and then the third time you said you thought that it was the 21st of May but you were not sure of the date. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. This is related to two battles. The second battle, whether it was on the 22nd or sometime later, whether -- it seems to me it was the 29th, but during this period it was the third time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You anticipated my question again. I was going to ask you is it possible that that third battle was on the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. It is possible, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, do you now think that that's the date when the third battle was when you were in Lapusnik, the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm still saying it is possible because it was the biggest battle. I'm looking at it from the intensity, from its intensity. It was a bigger battle. The one -- the one around about the 29th, it was quite big.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in Lapusnik for that battle?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that after the 29th of May, you were concerned about the -- what you described as the euphoria, and you were concerned that --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were concerned that the KLA was vulnerable in Malisheva, that the Serb forces could move in and take that area.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know whether I got the right translation. The KLA was not unprotected, but the developments that took place -- Malisheva came under control without any military action. It was not a result of military operations. It was not the result of the KLA potential, but it's a copy -- it's a phenomenon that was copied from Lapusnik and so on. It was received with euphoria by the people. And I knew that the KLA did not have the potential to defend Malisheve from the Serb forces if it was attacked. That was what it was in relation to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. So your testimony is that you were concerned about this euphoria.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that Mr. Limaj be shown Prosecution Exhibit 37, please. And with some luck it will be put up on the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, do you recall giving an interview to the Tirana television network on around the 3rd of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the document that's been put in front of you, Prosecution Exhibit 37, that's a transcription of that interview; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm just going to read from the -- from the document certain portions. At the beginning it says: "An interview with Mr. Celiku, one of the liberation army of Kosovo UCK commanders in one area of Drenica." And the question that's put to you: "Commander, can you please tell us something about the resistance that the UCK guerrilla units are putting up in the area you cover." And your answer is: "The UCK is an organised force and enjoys great support both in Drenica and in all the other areas of Kosova that are gripped by the war. Our army assisted by the local population, is putting up strong resistance to the enemy." You said that, right, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was true, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If you want me, I will comment all the statement. I cannot bring the context out of this little clip how we came to this and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I was -- I wanted to take it one step at a time. So you say here that "The UCK is an organised force and enjoys great support both in Drenica and all other areas of Kosova that are gripped by the war." That's what you said and that was true, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is not true. This is the first time that a member of the KLA had spoke on television. There had been statements here and there, but first time someone appeared with his face on television, it was me, and that was in the Albanian national television, and that was a programme about the diaspora, about Kosova. And for that time, in that interview, a member of the KLA, I could have used even bigger words to describe the KLA. And this was, Mr. Prosecutor, this was after the battle in Lapusnik. It was a big battle. We won that battle. And after that battle, as a result of this battle, we came to this interview, and that was the cue. That was the peg for that interview. And it was the resistance in that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you're telling us now what you said here in this interview was not true?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters correction: It was an interview with no image, only sound.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What are you expecting from a commander? It was the first time to talk about the KLA, and that was the first time -- the first opportunity to present the KLA, and it was the first time I was appearing on a public media. And this -- this is where the -- the pseudonym Celiku has been used. And if you consider my position at the time, it was the first time and I wanted to present the KLA in the best possible image, and that's what I've done. If -- the reality wasn't the same, but we wanted it to be like that, and we wanted to present the KLA in the best possible way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is that you inflated the situation, that what you said here was not true. That's your testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. It was inflated. The situation was inflated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what about this sentence: "Our army assist by the the local population is putting up strong resistance to the enemy"? That was true, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The population has assisted. There are certain things which are realistic, because the civilians have taken part in various actions in Lapusnik. Most of the people were villagers there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But "putting up strong resistance to the enemy"? I'll repeat my question. The army was putting up strong resistance to the enemy. That's true; right?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that battle of Lapusnik, we have offered the resistance that I've described. It was -- it was seen. That was -- it was a frontal action. It was the first real battle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or else --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question is: "Could tell us something about the actual results of this resistance?" And your answer is: "The greater part of Drenica territory and of Llapushe in general is free and under the control of our forces, that is, under the UCK's control. Our forces have had control of the Pristina-Peja highway for one month now, starting with the --"

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't seem to have this part here. You haven't given that to me. I've only got this one. If you can give me that page where the quote is. All I've got is a very short script. I've only got four paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't have a question, "Can you tell us something about the actual results of this resistance"? That question doesn't appear on your copy?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does -- does this --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this statement appear "The greater part of the Drenica territory and of Llapushe in general is free and under the control --" is that text --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll leave this, then, and we'll get a better translation for you to put these questions to you. Now, Mr. Limaj, the -- the seizure of the -- taking control of the Peja-Pristina road at Lapusnik, that was strategically very significant for the KLA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later developments showed what you're saying now, that it was strategically important. But when we had that battle, we were not thinking about the events as they would go in the future. We just wanted to stop the Serbs. We had this military action and then returned to our bases. But of course later it was strategically important. We realised that. But at that time we couldn't even imagine that the Serbian police not be able to -- would tolerate the blocking of that road by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, I'm just going to put to you what Sylejman Selimi said about this in his testimony here. He said, "Our strategy for the area was to have a free corridor and to be able to have this corridor for transporting weapons for the KLA." That's true. It was recognised as being an important spot to take control in order to transport weapons into the territories controlled by the KLA. Isn't that right, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, please look at the way we participated in that action. It shows how true that was. I am speaking about myself, what we did there. What other units did, I don't know. Maybe Mr. Selimi had such plans. In fact, we went there and I was wounded. I could hardly use my arm. Whether the other people had planned it or had prepared for it -- if you look at the events, they speak about a different truth because the units when we went there to help, to assist them, they were not in the Lapusnik gorge. The fighting was in Gjurgjice, Mr. Prosecutor, and Orlat, towards Mr. Krasniqi's place of birth, and I think at that time we didn't even think what the result of that battle would be. And in fact, as I said, the fighting started in Gjurgjice. I don't think there was planning or any preparation, but of course we developed further as the KLA and with the help of God we achieved what we wanted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you acknowledged that on the 9th of May battle at Lapusnik it was not just your unit but there were other units participating in that fighting; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, the fighting was going on in Gjurgjice and Orlat, and then later a unit from Poterk came. Poterk is a neighbourhood in Lapusnik. And this neighbourhood -- because the Serbian forces were all along the road from Gjurgjice to Lapusnik. They had some distance between them, but this unit from Poterk came to join and help the soldiers who were fighting in Gjurgjice while us --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that unit -- I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. Limaj, but that unit was from the other side of the Peja-Pristina road; correct, not your side?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was from --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so ultimately when the fighting moved to Lapusnik there was -- there were several units from different places involved in the fighting; correct? Not just your unit but there were other units involved in the fighting in Lapusnik; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The development of the situation later, the fighting started in Gjurgjice, and this unit from Poterk that was attacking the Serbian forces, there were civilians there, volunteers from everywhere, from various villages. For example, we were supported by civilians as well. I don't know how many there were. I have no idea how many came to join at that moment. But the main development or the main battle or the main fighting was there. It was not during one day. It was a battle that carried on from previous days because the Serbian forces wanted to penetrate that village to go into Gjurgjice to raid the village. That's why the fighting started there. And the unit that went to help there, they did not allow the Serbian forces to get into the village. And then on the third day happened what you mentioned in Lapusnik, when we went there. But the first two days the fighting was not very intense. It was of low intensity. And the Serbians -- the Serbs maybe did not think that we would resist that much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, if we could return to my question. My question was when the fighting moved to Lapusnik on the third day, on the 9th of May, there were not just your unit involved but there were other KLA units involved from other places; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, there were villagers, soldiers, various units. I did not know where they came from, but there were many who took part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever heard about it, they came to join.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just like us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you shown three exhibits at one time, Prosecution Exhibit 119, Prosecution Exhibit 159, Prosecution Exhibit 154.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- oh, I'm sorry. If you could look first at 154. Mr. Limaj, looking at Prosecution Exhibit 154, you see the line that is drawn in the area -- in the upper left-hand corner of the exhibit? Do you see that? Yes.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was drawn by Ramiz Qeriqi in his interview of the 23rd of April, 2003, and adopted by him in court. And what he said in court about it was that during May and June of 1998, this was the area -- the area inside of this line was the area that was under the control of Klecka, under the command of Klecka and that you were the person in charge in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wait for my question. That's true, isn't it, that this was the area under the command of Klecka in May and June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I can't remember Ramiz saying what you're saying here. Maybe I've forgotten it, but it's not true. Absolutely it's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What territory can you speak about? What zone can you speak about when you have only three or four people only? We didn't even talk about such things. We were only three or four or five, maximum, members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please focus on the question because we're talking about May and June of 1998, not -- well past the time when there were three or four. Okay? But you still say that it's not true for May and June? Okay.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such a definition is absolutely not true. Part of it is what happened after August. This happened after August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we look at Prosecution Exhibit 119, please. Do you have 119 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this was -- this drawing was drawn on the 25th of April, 2003, during an interview with Mr. Ramadan Behluli, which is now in evidence as Prosecution Exhibit 119. And what Mr. Behluli said when he drew this line, which appears on this map, is that this was the area of responsibility for Klecke in July of 1998 and that you were the commander in Klecka. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Behluli himself said that he was not focusing on the time. But this is not true, Your Honours. Mr. Prosecutor, it was impossible at that time. This is impossible. What you're trying to prove here is impossible. These are things that are not true about the time that we're talking about. If it were, I would have said it, but it wasn't. You're trying to prove something that was not true about Klecka at that time. As I said, many people had different ideas about what was going on May, June, July, but if you speak about zones, territories, commands, responsibilities, you can speak about those things only after August. And this is the truth, Mr. Prosecutor. Personally, there is nothing that -- I'm not trying here to avoid the truth. I know myself, and I have no reason to try to escape responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could look, Mr. Limaj, please, at Prosecution Exhibit P159. This is a diagram that was drawn by Shukri Buja during his interview on the 28th of April, 2003. So all three exhibits drawn in the same -- roughly the same week period -- week-long period in April 2003. And in Prosecution Exhibit 159, which is the interview with Shukri Buja which is now in evidence, he described this chart as being the points that were under the command of Klecka in May and June of 1998, and he's put your name along with Kumanova in the centre at Klecka. That's true, isn't it, Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Let's comment on this diagram, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's me just --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony is that all three diagrams are wrong.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way they are represented here now, they are not true. Shukri tried to explain what was going on here. I was in Klecke. You see here it's the General Staff. And where is the General Staff? It's not outside Klecke. Of course I was commander in Klecke but where is the place of the General Staff? It's in Klecke of course. But the General Staff was the highest body in the organisation. But this was not explained up to the end. We did not get to the bottom of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you recall of course that -- from seeing the clips of Mr. Shukri Buja's interview you recall that he --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- he drew the General Staff there not because it was in some other place in Klecka but because it was above your command in Klecka. You recall that, don't you Mr. Limaj?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember his interview very well but not the way you're explaining it now. Many things -- about many things that he said there he has been pushed. He was pushed by you. He said that he never took orders from me, he had in connection with Klecka while you tried to prove the opposite. He said he never took orders from Klecka and now you have this diagram here. I think Shukri explained what he was trying to say. And here I'm saying the truth as I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just intervene again? I'm sorry to keep doing it, but if I may say so, it's completely pointless to select parts of a witness's evidence - of course I can do it in re-examination, of course I can do it in a final brief - but essentially what should be put, if we're going to go down this road in the case of all those three witnesses is the qualifications they've made to the evidence they've made. What view you take about it in the long run, of course, is another matter, but to select part of it and then say to the witness, "Well that's true, isn't it," we say once again it is totally improper and it is wasting time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I certainly would share your view that there is a lack of concern for timeliness about these matters, Mr. Mansfield, and you can be well sure that we, as is your client it would appear, he having heard the evidence and studied it closely, are well aware of the differences in account, and because of that the concerns you express are not going to have the effects that you are putting by way of submission might be taken in respect of this. Bear in mind that your client was present throughout the evidence of these witnesses. It's not as though he is a witness who has no knowledge of what was said in this court. For that reason, we are not interfering at this point, but I'm sure that Mr. Whiting has heard and needed to be reminded what has been said and will take account of it as he pursues his cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, for my next question I'm going to have to give you a chart, and it's of the protected witnesses and their pseudonyms who testified in this case. Because if I make reference to protected witnesses I have to do it by pseudonym, but I can't expect you to remember all their pseudonyms. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't know if the Court or Defence counsel need copies of this chart. I'm seeing nods from the Defence -- no. I'm seeing nods and shaking of head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, looking at the chart you see Witness L95?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recall his testimony?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall meeting him at the end of July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember meeting him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was in Novoselle?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. He was confused. After the offensive from Malisheve, from Lapusnik. People did not know where they were going. It could have been Novoselle or Klecka. They were there, and I found them a place where to stay. Maybe I met them at the place they were staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, tell us where you remember meeting them. Where is it that you remember meeting this witness?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult for me to remember the exact place, whether we met on the road or whether we went to the house where they were staying. Really, it's difficult for me to remember, but I believe I met this person and not only once but two or throw times. I don't know exactly where the first meeting took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But -- I understand you don't remember exactly where it took place, but do you remember that it took place in Novoselle?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it took place either the day that Lapusnik fell on the 26th of July or a day before or a day after; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could be mistaken here as well about the precise date because the developments on the 25th, 26th, and 27th were such. But it should be the 27th or 28th. It could be the 26th as well, but I'm not sure of the date. Those were horrific developments. It wasn't anything particular for me to remember. I'm not sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told him that if he needed anything that he should come to Klecke?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. After they settled there, I told them, "Whatever you need," meaning food or something else, I told them, "You can come and report to Klecka."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told him that he was in charge there. He would be in charge of the soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they came, but it seems that I received a message from his commander, a coded message, and I had to convey that message to him. So I just conveyed a message coming from his leader. Because it was a Dukadjini unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, you said you received a coded message. How was this message relayed to you, by what means?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, I think that those young men, they were in those parts, in Malisheve, after the developments in Malisheve, and one of the soldiers, now I don't remember whether he was one of my soldiers who brought me that message. He brought me a letter. This is how it

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could avoid mentioning the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if there could be a redaction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Limaj, so your testimony is that the message was conveyed by letter and it was in code.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't coded. Name, last name, message from this person. This young man, tell him that he is in charge of that group. Do this for me because I cannot come there, and that was it. So he said he wasn't able to come, which means that he planned to come but he couldn't. So he said that until I came there, tell this soldier that he was responsible and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just -- at line 9 of page 79 on the transcript here you said that "I received a message from his commander, a coded message." Now, are you saying now that --

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that misinterpretation or did you misspeak?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This might be a mistake with the interpretation. I didn't say a coded message. I said a message. I didn't use a "coded message." To tell you the truth even today I don't know what a coded message looks like and how these coded messages are compiled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had another occasion to meet this person, this witness, and that was in your headquarters in Klecka a couple of days later, one or two days later; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met him. And I can tell you what he said, although I don't remember, because it is possible that he came to Klecka and that he met me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the occasion when he met you there were various unit commanders -- Isak Musliu, Kumanova, Shukri Buja -- who were there and you were -- you were holding a meeting and they were reporting to you, or at least Shukri Buja and Kumanova were reporting to you at that meeting. Is that correct? Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor. Your Honours, this is not true. We had no place to stay at that time. It's quite normal that Isak and other soldiers stayed with us together in Klecke. We drank tea together. Even Shukri had no other place to go because the Serb forces penetrated his village and his soldiers, they all came to Klecke. What reports are we talking here about? We just had a free discussion. We drank tea. We had an ordinary conversation. This is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were not in charge of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no meeting, Mr. Prosecutor. What you call a meeting, meetings that we held in Klecka are different, and this person you're referring to, he did not participate in such meetings. He just happened to be in the zone and then went back to his own zone. There is no reason for him to be part of such a meeting on the 5th of August or before the 5th of August. But this was when they would come to Klecka to get clothes or cigarettes. Usually they came for cigarettes. Then this person sat down with us. And all these soldiers, as I said, we were under a Serb offensive, and all the soldiers in these parts were there. So his interpretation -- his interpretation does not stand. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the witness to slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May we know which witness it is being suggested indicated that Fatmir Limaj was in charge of this meeting so that this can be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's -- it's Witness L95, and it's -- the reference is Day 49, page 4218.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you heard, Mr. Limaj, that you were speeding up there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I'm doing my best not to speed up, but I tend to forget.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, going back to June and July of 1998, there was -- during those months there was fighting in various places like -- you can put those aside, or perhaps the usher can take them. During June and July of 1998, there was fighting in various places like Carraleve, Blinaje, Luzhnice. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were fightings on these points that you're mentioning and in other parts as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During May, June, and July of 1998 was there any fighting in Klecka?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't any fighting in Klecka, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't think so. Now, the fighting in Carraleve was on -- you recall were on the 14th, 17th, and 21st approximately of June.

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember the dates. In Duhle I think it was the 1st or the 2nd when they came out publicly, and I don't remember the dates about the other fightings. There were confrontations from time to time, but I don't remember the other fightings except for the second one and the last one on the 25th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the fighting that occurred in Luzhnice around the 25th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but there was fighting in Luzhnice on several occasions. There is a location there called Bajrak, and, Your Honours, the Serbian forces there like in Cuka, they used this area for their dislocation. The Serb forces tried on several occasions to penetrate the village, and that's why there were several fightings with these forces. And the Duhle gorge, as in other places, the Serbian police made use of some bases that were formerly used by the Yugoslav army. And that's why I'm saying that there were several fightings in Luznica every now and then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When there is fighting in these various places like in Carraleve and in Luzhnice, for example, units from other places would go to assist in the fighting; correct?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers from different units, depending on where they heard about the fighting, they went to assist, and this began after the units became public. And first it functioned when one friend informed another, and this is what happened with all KLA units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on -- at times the assistance of one unit to another unit would be coordinated by Klecka, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never such a case, Mr. Prosecutor. If there was from Klecka -- for example, let's say there were two fightings. One group would go to one and the other to the other place. But what you're saying, that it was coordinated by Klecka, that is not true. This was a responsibility that the soldiers felt for themselves. Whoever felt that he has this need to go and assist the others, they went, but it wasn't coordinated by Klecka. And we were not in a position to coordinate them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall sending or instructing Ramiz Qeriqi and some other soldiers, in June of 1998, to go assist in fighting that was occurring near Rahovec in a village called Rakovc? Do you recall doing that?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. This is not true. The truth is different, and I will tell you that. The developments in Rakovc/Rahovec, Luan was in his traditional clothes. He came to Klecke for a visit. He was on his way to Malisheve for oil. We were getting ready and we asked him, Are you coming with us and he said no. And this was it. This is not true what you're saying, that someone sent someone to Kroimire. This is not true. It was a free choice, Mr. Prosecutor. You could not tell us so, go here or help this unit. At -- in Klecka, to tell you the truth, you could tell the soldier you can go here, you can go there, but at Kroimire, no. At that time, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About Luan go from that location to Rakovc? Just yes or no. Did he go from Klecka to Rakovc on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FATMIR LIMAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did, but I don't know. To tell you the truth, I don't know. I might make a mistake. It wasn't something special for me to remember. Things like that happened on a daily basis. For example, someone would go to Malisheve to his own house for a visit and then he would find himself in a battle and stay there for three days and nobody knew where he was. This was something that was going on every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, one matter. Perhaps overnight my learned friend can check the transcript reference that he gave. Looking at the official court transcript, the citation of which my learned friend gave, there is no reference whatsoever that could possibly support, in my submission, the question that was put. The only reference I can find, perhaps my learned friend can consider it overnight, is page 4235 in which that particular witness is asked about the meeting and all he says that Celiku asked everyone to speak about the problems but this does not mean that he took the floor first. But I can't find anything in the transcripts in which it's said by the witness that that meeting was headed by Mr. Limaj or that he was chairing the meeting. I ask that my learned friend study that matter and perhaps clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Khan. We will adjourn now until 2.15 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
